content:
Recurring Receipt

Create receipts that repeat on a regular schedule.

Useful for regular customer payments like monthly subscriptions or rent income.

Next issue date

The date when the next receipt will be automatically created. This date advances automatically based on your frequency settings.

Set this to match when you expect to receive payments. For example, if rent is collected on the 1st, set this to the 1st.

Interval

The frequency interval for creating receipts. This number works with the period type to match your income schedule.

Common examples: 1 Month = monthly income, 1 Week = weekly collections, 3 Months = quarterly dividends, 1 Year = annual fees.

PeriodType

The period type that works with the interval to determine frequency. Select the unit of time for your income cycle.

Most recurring income is received monthly, but adjust this to match your actual collection schedule.

MonthDay

For monthly recurring receipts, specify which day of the month the receipt should be created.

Match this to when payments are typically received. For rent collected on the 1st, select '1st day of month'.

ExpirationType

Determines when the recurring schedule ends. This controls how long the system will continue creating receipts.

Choose 'Until further notice' for indefinite income like rent, or 'Until date' for fixed-term contracts.

UntilDate

The date when recurring receipts will stop being created. The system will not create any receipts after this date.

Use this for fixed-term leases, time-limited contracts, or any income stream with a known end date.

Paid by

The type of payer making the payment. This determines which contact list to select from.

Choose Customer for most business income, Supplier for supplier refunds or rebates, or Other for non-business income.

Customer

Select the customer making the payment. This links the receipt to their account for tracking.

This is typically used for regular customer payments, rent from tenants, or subscription fees.

Supplier

Select the supplier making the payment. This links the receipt to their account for tracking.

Supplier receipts might include rebates, refunds, or commission income from suppliers.

Contact

Enter the name of the payer when they're not in your customer or supplier lists.

Use this for one-time payers or personal income. Consider adding regular payers as customers for better tracking.

Received in

The bank or cash account that will receive the payment. This account will be debited (increased) for each receipt.

Select the account where you typically deposit this type of income. The currency of this account determines the receipt currency.

Cleared

The clearing status for bank transactions. Controls whether receipts appear as pending or cleared in bank reconciliation.

Use 'Pending' if payments need to clear through the bank, or 'Cleared' for immediate deposits like cash or electronic transfers.

Description

A description that identifies this recurring receipt and will be copied to each generated receipt.

Be specific to help identify the income source. Examples: 'Monthly rent - Unit 5', 'Weekly service fee', 'Quarterly dividend income'.

Lines

The receipt lines specifying which accounts to credit and the amounts. These lines will be copied to each generated receipt.

Add a line for each income category or account affected by this receipt. The total of all lines equals the receipt amount.

If amounts vary, you'll need to edit individual receipts after they're created or update this template.

Automatic reference

When enabled, the system automatically assigns sequential reference numbers to each generated receipt.

Recommended for maintaining a clear audit trail of all income. You can still add receipt details in the description field.
